newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Up to 800 flee attacks in southwest Angola.
newsitem.headline: Up to 800 flee attacks in southwest Angola.

text.p: Up to 800 Angolans have fled attacks by armed men in the southwest of the southern African country in the last week, United Nations and aid sources said on Wednesday.
"We have a report of an estimated 250 men attacking the town of Calohombo in Benguela province," David Wimhurst, spokesman for the U.N. Verification Mission in Angola, told Reuters.

"As a result of this attack, 700 to 800 people have fled the area to Cubal," Wimhurst said, referring to the city in Benguela already home to over 120,000 refugees displaced by Angola's two- decade-long civil war.
Wimhurst said the attackers appeared to be armed bandits, although other sources in the capital Luanda reported supporters of the former rebel UNITA movement were responsible.

The area around Cubal has been the scene of growing violence in recent months. Different groups -- some with ties to UNITA, others to the government and bandits -- have attacked villages in the region, according to aid workers in the area.
The medical group Medecins Sans Frontieres reported that fighting broke out between members of UNITA and government- backed civil defence forces last weekend.
UNITA and the government signed a peace accord in 1994 which has brought Angola the longest period of relative peace since the civil war erupted at independence from Portugal in 1975.

A new unity government is expected to be inaugurated on March 20. The U.N. has 6,638 troops, military observers and civilian police from more than 30 countries in Angola, helping to implement the peace accord.
